tess-support: FYI — customer ACME (ticket ACME-1423) seeing sporadic embedding dim mismatch on /v1/embeddings. They expect 1024 dims but intermittently get 1536. Downstream pipeline fails. Seen ~5 occurrences across 2h. Repro in ticket.

mike-ml: can you paste minimal repro + model name + auth token id? we need the routing key to check fallbacks. :mag_right:

tess-support: excerpt from their curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED-ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-compact-1024","input":["a","b","c"],"max_batch_size":128}'
```

They run from us-west, sustained QPS ~140 with short bursts to 300. They set max_batch_size=128. Report says mismatch aligns with bursts.

maya-eng: quick thought — our dynamic coalescer may be combining requests and routing to a compatible higher-dim variant (embed-wide-1536) under shard pressure. If responses from fallback variant come back, client will receive 1536 dims. We've seen a similar pattern but different models.

ravi-sre: from infra logs (summary): between 2025-03-14T21:10-21:18 UTC, we had ~11k embed requests and 76 fallback events where embed-compact-1024 routed to embed-wide-1536 due to hot shards. Several GPUs (gpunode-07, gpunode-19) showed GC spikes. Snippet:

```
[21:12:04] coalesce size=144 request_model=embed-compact-1024 routed_to=embed-wide-1536
[21:12:04] enqueue_ms=980 process_ms=1800 node=gpunode-19 gc_ms=290
```

mike-ml: can you run a repro script that hits max_batch_size=128 and simulates bursts? I can try to reproduce in staging.

maya-eng: ran local load test: 200rps sustained with intermittent 2s bursts. After ~70s I saw a 1536-dim response returned to a request for embed-compact-1024. Config used: dynamic batching enabled, routing_policy=balanced. Repro steps:
- start multi-threaded load gen (python requests)
- send batches of 8 inputs, set max_batch_size=128
- observe responses and assert dims

log from repro:
```
[00:01:10] batch_coalesce size=136 models=[embed-compact-1024] -> fallback=embed-wide-1536
[00:01:10] response_dims=1536 for request_id=stg-req-442
```

mike-ml: root cause wfm: (1) routing fallback to larger-dim variant under shard saturation, (2) coalescer currently permits merging requests that only differ by variant compatibility without validating final response dims before returning to client.

ravi-sre: short-term mitigations to propose to customer:
- pin exact variant with version (e.g., `embed-compact-1024@v7`) or set `routing_policy=strict`
- reduce `max_batch_size` (<=64) to limit coalesced batch growth
- if critical, move to Dedicated pool to avoid cross-tenant fallbacks

mike-ml: infra-side quick actions:
- add response-dim validation at edge: if returned dim != expected based on requested model signature, return 500 + diagnostic header and log event
- add alert: coalesced_batch_size > 120 AND fallback_count > 3/min
- short-term canary: enable strict-dim-check in coalescer on 10% of us-west traffic

deploy-bot: canary deployed: `coalescer-dimcheck=v2-canary` -> prod-us-west 10% (deploy id dpl-8943). Monitoring enabled.

maya-eng: I'll open PR to make coalescer refuse to merge requests where final_variant_dim != requested_model_dim unless explicit compatibility override is set. Also adding per-request field `expected_embedding_dim` optional for clients to enforce.

tess-support: updated customer with workarounds (pin variant + lower max_batch_size + ETA). Customer asked for ETA/impact and requested logs. Escalated to enterprise support (ACME-1423-ESC). They want a fix timeline.

mike-ml: timeline: if canary stable for 30m with no regressions, we can promote to 100% in ~45m. I'll monitor metrics (fallbacks, p99 latency, error rate).

ravi-sre: additional note — autoscaler tuning: during short spikes we allowed fallbacks rather than spinning new shards; long-term we'll tweak scale-up aggressiveness for embedding pools to avoid noisy fallbacks.

tess-support: thanks team — keeping ACME updated. I'll attach repro and logs to ACME-1423 and follow up after canary window. :white_check_mark:
